mcp.title: Connect MCP services
mcp.lead: Agents reference MCP servers that run through the registry gateway. Two connection paths exist — the universal caller-key path and the client-native OAuth discovery path.

keyPath.title: Caller key (universal)
keyPath.body: Mint a wgk- caller key in the registry console; the CLI verifies it and stores it locally (0600). After that, install can write each target's native MCP configuration carrying that key.
keyPath.mintNote: Mint keys in the registry console:

oauthPath.title: OAuth discovery (client-native)
oauthPath.body: The registry answers unauthenticated MCP requests with a WWW-Authenticate header pointing at its protected-resource metadata, and serves the standard discovery documents — clients that support OAuth discovery can complete authorization in the browser.
oauthPath.honest: Whether the connection completes with zero manual entry depends on your client's own OAuth support; dynamic client registration is not offered.

essentials.title: Essentials
essentials.quota: Calls are free within the monthly free quota; over-quota calls are refused with 402 and reset next month.
essentials.tier: Paid-tier servers (e.g. law-bench) refuse community keys with an upgrade prompt naming the tier.
essentials.revoke: Keys can be revoked in the registry console at any time; the local copy can be cleared from the CLI.

create.title: Create and publish an agent
create.lead: Publishing requires the creators group. Three authoring routes exist; all of them end at the same publish gate, and published versions are immutable.
create.route1: In 壹座: Settings → Agents → New agent — compose skills, MCP references, and personas as a draft.
create.route2: One-click conversion: turn a custom preset into an agent draft (Settings → Custom presets → Publish), with a report of what was carried and what needs replacing.
create.route3: From the creator console (#/mine): submit an agent manifest directly to the publish endpoint; validation errors surface verbatim.
create.versions: Every publish appends an immutable version; each version may carry a short note (≤500 characters).
create.subscribe: Subscribe and install are two acts: a subscription is recorded in the market; installing takes a definite version snapshot.
create.gate: Only registry-registered MCP servers can be referenced; agent entries are persona-only.

detail.selfhostTitle: Deploy this agent on the official cloud
detail.selfhostBody: This self-hosted instance doesn't run agent serving. To put this agent's roles online — shareable pages, metered turns, earnings — publish it to the official marketplace; the one-click deploy flow runs there.
detail.selfhostNote: Self-hosting the serving stack yourself is possible — see the repository docs; the marketplace route needs no extra infrastructure.
detail.deploySummary: Deploying takes the roles inside this agent and puts them live as a conversation service: you get a shareable public chat page, visitors are metered per round, and you (the deployer) take a revenue share.
detail.keySubtitle: Metering key = the quota that pays for visitor rounds: visitors chat free, rounds are billed to the key you paste here.
detail.rhythmSubtitle: Rhythm = whether it works on its own: no entries means it only answers when addressed; entries have the platform wake it on schedule (spending your quota).
detail.modelSubtitle: Model = which model it thinks with: empty keeps the standing setting (an existing override, else the agent's declared default).
detail.budgetSubtitle: Budget = how long one round may run: empty keeps the standing setting (an existing override, else the declared ceiling or the platform default).

narrative.title: Platform infrastructure vs agent content
narrative.body: MCP servers and skills on this page are platform-provided infrastructure: connect them to your MCP client or agent and use them directly. An Agent is a content bundle that combines skills, MCP references, and personas into one installable unit — install it and its parts arrive together.
